findings.detail: Under IAS 28 the equity method does not bring an associate's revenue into the consolidated income statement (only share of profit). The ADR's 'equity_share' basis therefore represents a management/operational attribution metric rather than a disclosed IFRS line. The ADR's treatment is correct — rejecting re-discounting of equity_share revenue at the apply_ownership_share layer is precisely the right anti-double-counting design — but a one-line clarification in §3/§4 (equity-share revenue is a model/operational metric, not a consolidated financial-statement line) would prevent future misreading.
findings.title: equity_share basis is an operational metric, not an IFRS income-statement line

findings.detail: IFRS 3 requires recognizing the acquiree's results from the acquisition date; the ADR's allow_pro_rata day-weighting across a period is a defensible model approximation of that rule (and default-rejecting silent averaging is the right conservative default). Recommend one sentence in §4 noting this is a modeling simplification of acquisition-date accounting, not an IFRS 3 election.
findings.title: day-weighted pro-rata is a model approximation of IFRS 3 acquisition-date recognition
